items.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing and health-related quality of life in children with idiopathic or heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension.
items.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease causing elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular (RV) failure, and premature death. Idiopathic and heritable PAH impair functional capacity and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) assesses exercise limitation and disease severity, yet its relationship with HRQoL has not been investigated in pediatric PAH. A retrospective multicenter study across three French tertiary pediatric cardiology centers was conducted (June 2023-April 2025). Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH who underwent CPET and completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL 4.0) were included. Key CPET parameters were analyzed, and associations to HRQoL scores assessed via Spearman correlation. Among 19 children (median age 11 years, median follow-up 32 months), exercise capacity was reduced (peak VO2 29 ml/kg/min; 74.5% predicted; Z-score -2.9), with ventilatory inefficiency (VE/VCO₂ slope 40). QoL scores were lower than normative values. No significant correlation was found between CPET parameters and HRQoL scores. Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH present exercise limitation and impaired HRQoL, though CPET parameters were not correlated with HRQoL scores, reflecting limited statistical power. Larger studies are needed to clarify this relationship.

items.title: Colchicine use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic gout without prior coronary artery disease: A propensity-matched nationwide cohort study.
items.abstract: Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.52% of colchicine users versus 15.03% of non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.75; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly reduced in colchicine users (8.01% vs. 11.07%; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.53-0.62; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.96-1.37; P = 0.121) or stroke (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.81-1.01; P = 0.076). In a landmark analysis at 365 days that addressed immortal time bias, the associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.62-0.73; P < 0.001) and with the composite outcome (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.71-0.81; P < 0.001) remained significant, whereas stroke (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.87-1.12; P = 0.823) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.95-1.40; P = 0.144) did not differ between the two groups. In patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease, colchicine use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The reduction in the composite outcome was driven by mortality rather than by myocardial infarction or stroke.

items.title: Associations of dietary inflammatory index with incident cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality in patients with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A prospective study of data from the UK Biobank.
items.abstract: While the dietary inflammatory index (DII) is linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality in the general population, its role in individuals with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains understudied. Given the elevated inflammatory burden in this high-risk group, we aimed to examine the association between energy-adjusted DII (E-DII) and incident cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality using a prospective cohort from the UK Biobank. We conducted a prospective cohort study using UK Biobank data, including 18,193 individuals with prediabetes and 6,469 with T2D, all free of cardiovascular disease and cancer at baseline. The E-DII was derived from 24-hour dietary recall data, incident CVD and all-cause mortality were ascertained through linked hospital and death records. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with a median duration of 12.2 years (IQR: 11.5-13.0). Among participants with T2D, an energy-adjusted DII > 1 (vs. ≥-1 to ≤1) was associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.00-1.53) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.01-1.84). The association with cardiovascular mortality was not statistically significant (HR 1.50, 95% CI 0.76-2.94). No significant associations were observed among participants with prediabetes. A more pro-inflammatory dietary pattern, as measured by the E-DII, is independently associated with increased risks of incident cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in individuals with T2D. These findings support the integration of DII into nutritional risk assessment for diabetic populations and highlight the potential of dietary modification to improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: Development and validation of an explainable artificial intelligence model to predict in-hospital adverse events for patients with acute myocardial infarction.
items.abstract: In-hospital adverse events after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) can occur abruptly and adversely affect short-term prognosis. We developed and externally validated explainable machine learning models to predict a composite of in-hospital atrial fibrillation (AF), ventricular fibrillation (VF), cardiac arrest (CA), or death using routinely available admission data. We retrospectively analyzed 7,496 patients from the MIMIC-IV database as the development cohort and 2,776 patients from Xuanwu Hospital as the external validation cohort. Predictors included demographics, medical history, and admission laboratory tests. Logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron, and TabNet models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using discrimination, classification, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Latent class analysis identified three outcome clusters with distinct event-probability profiles. XGBoost achieved the best performance for the composite outcome in the development cohort (AUROC, 0.798). Predictive performance was moderate to good for AF and in-hospital death, with AUROCs of up to 0.834 and 0.870 in the development cohort and 0.803 and 0.849 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Discrimination was lower for VF and CA. SHapley Additive exPlanations highlighted neutrophil and leukocyte counts, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, renal function, glucose, glycated hemoglobin A1c, and prior AF as important predictors. These explainable models may support early risk stratification and help guide monitoring intensity and timely intervention in patients with AMI.

items.title: Genetic determinants of direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) response: evidence, limitations and barriers to clinical implementation.
items.abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) offer predictable pharmacokinetics and simplified dosing compared with warfarin, yet clinically important inter-individual variability in drug exposure, efficacy and safety persists. Pharmacogenomics can help explain this variability and advance precision anticoagulation. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on genetic determinants of the pharmacokinetics and clinical outcomes of dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban, identified by searching PubMed, Embase and Web of Science from inception to May 2026. Evidence from candidate-gene studies, genome-wide association studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses was synthesized and the magnitude of reported genetic effects were compared the non-genetic determinants of exposure. Variants in CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CES1, ABCB1 and ABCG2 have been investigated for their potential effects on DOAC disposition and response. CES1 variants, particularly rs2244613, rs8192935 and rs71647871, may influence dabigatran exposure, while transporter variants may affect absorption and elimination. CYP3A4/5 and ABCG2 variation has also been associated with altered rivaroxaban and apixaban pharmacokinetics. Evidence for edoxaban, including SLCO1B1 variation, remains limited. Pharmacogenomics represents a promising component of individualized DOAC therapy, but routine clinical implementation is in progress. Prospective genotype-guided studies, validated polygenic and clinical-genetic scores, therapeutic concentration thresholds and diverse multiethnic validation are needed before pharmacogenomic testing can reliably inform DOAC selection and dosing.

items.title: Multiple Sclerosis Relapses Are Associated With EBV-Specific T-Cell Expansion Amid Broad Immune Activation.
items.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is strongly implicated in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet the mechanisms linking EBV to disease pathogenesis remain unclear. EBV-specific T cells are hypothesized to contribute to MS through molecular mimicry. We aimed to investigate the relationship between EBV-specific T cells and MS relapses using longitudinal T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire profiling. We analyzed TCR repertoires from sequential peripheral blood samples collected before and after relapses in 5 patients with MS. CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were sorted into naive, memory, and regulatory subsets. TCR antigen specificity was determined using exact matches to public databases and GLIPH2-based clustering, covering EBV, cytomegalovirus, influenza, Mycobacterium tuberculosis , and self-antigens. The results were compared with those from healthy controls. At baseline, patients with MS showed a significant enrichment of EBV-specific TCRs within CD8 + T cells, comparable with patterns seen in other autoimmune diseases. After relapses, EBV-specific TCR frequencies markedly increased across all T-cell subsets. TCRs recognizing other viral antigens, including polyspecific TCRs with broad reactivity, displayed similar baseline enrichment and relapse-associated expansion patterns. Our findings indicate a temporal association between MS relapses, global immune activation, and EBV-specific T-cell expansions, which is consistent with a two-step model of MS relapse immunopathogenesis. An initial, unidentified trigger induces broad immune activation, promoting the expansion of antiviral T cells, including those specific to EBV. These EBV-specific and polyspecific T cells with heightened cross-reactivity may then contribute to MS relapses. Larger studies are needed to further define the role of T-cell dynamics in MS pathogenesis.

items.title: Bacteroidetes promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and resistance to immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Growing evidence highlights the gut microbiome's critical role in tumorigenesis and immunotherapy response. However, the impact of gut microbes on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains unclear due to the lack of combined preclinical and clinical studies. We performed 16S rRNA sequencing of cross-cohort stool samples from 10 HCC responders (R) and 40 non-responders (NR) to ICB at baseline and on-treatment time points. We identified Bacteroidetes enrichment in NR. To study the microbiome's role in cancer immune response, we generated an immunogenic mouse model of HCC via hydrodynamic tail-vein injection (HDTVI) of DNA plasmids mimicking common HCC alterations and immunogenicity by expressing OVA model antigens (MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 tumors). We found that antibiotic (ABX)-induced dysbiosis promoted a pro-tumorigenic effect in the MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 HCC and reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment by reducing dendritic cells (DCs) through the expansion of the Bacteroidetes species, Parabacteroides distasonis. P. distasonis colonization in mice harboring MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 liver tumors confirmed its pro-tumorigenic effect in vivo. Furthermore, fecal matter transplant of patient microbiotas into murine recipients demonstrated that microbiota from an NR donor enriched in Bacteroidetes promoted faster tumorigenesis compared with microbiota from an R donor with reduced Bacteroidetes. We isolated 6 Bacteroidetes species from the NR donor into a bacterial cocktail. After colonization with the Bacteroidetes cocktail, mice harboring MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 HCC exhibited increased tumorigenesis, reduced survival, and impaired response to ICB. This study identified Bacteroidetes enrichment as a potential biomarker of ICB resistance in HCC and, by using immunogenic mouse models, established that Bacteroidetes abundance influences tumor development and response to ICB.

items.title: Effects of COVID-19 vaccination type and vaccination-infection interval on viral clearance dynamics in Omicron BA.5 patients at Guangzhou Fangcang shelter hospitals: A propensity score matched multicenter retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: The Omicron BA.5 subvariant exhibited pronounced immune evasion and was associated with widespread breakthrough infections. Unlike settings where mRNA vaccines predominated, China mainly used inactivated vaccines, with the adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine Ad5-nCoV also administered at scale. Real-world evidence on post-infection viral clearance associated with these platforms remains limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 16,533 mild or asymptomatic Omicron BA.5 cases from two Fangcang shelter hospitals in Guangzhou, China, from Novernber 5 to December 8, 2022. The primary objective was to compare viral-clearance time between unvaccinated and vaccinated participants. The secondary objective was to compare inactivated-vaccine recipients, or and Ad5-nCoV recipients, containing regimens in a propensity score-matched cohort; the last-dose-to-infection interval analysis was exploratory. Propensity score matching was performed using age, sex, marital status, occupation, and province as covariates to improve between-group comparability. All patients underwent standardized daily RT-PCR testing containing both N and ORF1ab genes, with Ct values > 35 defined as negative. The outcome was time to viral clearance, defined as two consecutive negative nasopharyngeal swabs ≥ 24 hours apart. In the overall cohort, vaccinated patients had significantly shorter shedding duration (9.05 vs… 10.42d; P  < .001) compared with unvaccinated patients. The matched cohort included 228 unvaccinated, 228 inactivated vaccine recipients, and 114 Ad5-nCoV recipients. Median time to viral clearance differed across groups with 9.42, 8.56, and 8.48d, respectively. Prior vaccination was associated with shorter viral clearance but with no significant difference observed between inactivated vaccine and Ad5-nCoV recipients among the matched regimens.

items.title: The pore-forming protein APOL7C ruptures Leishmania major-containing parasitophorous vacuoles in dendritic cells to promote IL-12 production and the induction of T helper type 1 immunity.
items.abstract: Classical dendritic cells (cDCs) are required for the efficient priming of T helper type 1 (Th1) immunity against Leishmania major infections in mice. They do so by producing large quantities of IL-12 in response to L. major infection. IL-12 in turn supports the generation of protective CD4+ Th1 cells. However, the mechanism(s) by which L. major instigates robust IL-12 production by cDCs has not been addressed. Here we show that expression of a pore-forming protein called APOL7C is induced in cDCs by L. major infection. APOL7C is expressed in the cytosol of host cells and, remarkably, upon infection is recruited to L. major parasitophorous vacuoles (PVs) where it induces PV rupture. PV rupture leads to the exposure of L. major-derived pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) to cytosolic pattern recognition receptors (PRRs). Cytosolic PRR signaling then drives IL-12 production by cDCs. Consequently, L. major challenge of APOL7C-deficient mice results in reduced numbers of IL-12 producing cDCs as well as a diminished Th1 response. In sum, our data indicate the presence of pore-forming proteins in the cytosol of cDCs that interfere with the intracellular niche of Leishmania to modulate immunity to these parasites.

items.title: Combined monophosphoryl lipid A and alpha-Galactosyl ceramide adjuvants enhance the systemic immune response to intranasal inactivated influenza vaccination in a murine homologous challenge model.
items.abstract: Inactivated influenza vaccines (IIVs) often fail to provide robust mucosal protection, necessitating the development of potent adjuvants for intranasal delivery. This study evaluated a novel adjuvant combination of Monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL), a TLR4 agonist, and alpha-Galactosyl Ceramide (α-GalCer), an NKT cell ligand, to enhance the efficacy of an intranasal inactivated A/PR8 (iPR8) influenza vaccine. In vitro results demonstrated that MPL+ α-GalCer increased the frequencies of CD4⁺ CD25⁺ , CD8⁺ CD25⁺ and CD4⁺ CD69⁺ T cells relative to both the vehicle control and either single adjuvant in splenocyte cultures, whereas in purified dendritic cell and macrophage cultures MPL+ α-GalCer was no more effective than MPL alone. Splenocyte supernatants showed higher elevated TNF- α, IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-13. This pre-activation drove robust allogeneic T-cell proliferation in a mixed lymphocyte reaction, indicating enhanced allostimulatory capacity rather than influenza-specific priming. In vivo, a single intranasal dose of iPR8+ MPL+ α-GalCer elicited high systemic IgG titers and was effective at inducing Th1-associated IgG2a alongside IgG1. Following an LD50-range PR8 challenge, the combined-adjuvant group showed 100% survival, which was not statistically significant and lower lung viral titers at 7 days post-infection. This group exhibited elevated post-challenge lung-associated antigen-specific IgA and a reduced viral burden, which was accompanied by lower inflammatory cell infiltration and cytokine levels. The protection of combination group was accompanied by increased frequencies of ex vivo antigen-responsive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells recovered post-challenge. Our findings suggest that the MPL+ α-GalCer combination enhances innate and adaptive immune responses, providing an effective adjuvant platform for homologous mucosal protection in a murine model.

items.title: Serum ferritin kinetics and ferritin-derived ratios in hospitalised adults with dengue: A prospective serial biomarker study.
items.abstract: Dengue causes major morbidity and mortality across India, where early identification of patients progressing to dengue shock syndrome or severe hepatitis remains an unmet need. Serum ferritin reflects macrophage activation, but its serial kinetics and ferritin-derived composite indices have not been rigorously evaluated in adult Indian populations. We characterised serial ferritin kinetics and evaluated two ferritin-derived ratios: the Ferritin-to-Platelet Ratio (FPR) and the Ferritin/ALT Ratio (FLR). This prospective observational study enrolled 100 adult WHO 2009-confirmed dengue patients at SMIMER, Surat (June 2020-November 2021). Serum ferritin was measured by sandwich ELISA on hospital Days 1, 3 and 5 and was also analysed by day of illness; platelet count and transaminases were the lowest and highest values recorded during the stay, and outcomes were recorded if present at any time between admission and discharge. Severity was classified as non-severe (n = 68) or severe (n = 32). Non-circular endpoints-shock/DSS (n = 22), severe thrombocytopenia <20,000/μL (n = 28), and severe hepatitis AST/ALT ≥ 1,000 IU/L (n = 18)-were the primary outcomes for diagnostic accuracy. FPR and FLR were pre-specified composite indices and were compared with their component tests by paired DeLong tests. Ferritin showed a rise-peak-fall trajectory across hospital days, peaking on Day 3 (mean 955 ± 177 ng/ml; Friedman p < 10-16); by day of illness it rose from a median of 700 ng/ml (illness days ≤3) to 950 ng/ml (days 6-7) and then plateaued. FPR Day 1 separated the severity groups with AUC 0.704 (95% CI 0.579-0.830); severe patients showed five-fold higher median FPR than non-severe patients (39.0 vs 7.5; p = 0.001). Against shock/DSS, FPR Day 1 had AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.688-0.898), no higher than platelet count alone (AUC 0.784; DeLong p = 0.41). FLR Day 1 discriminated severe hepatitis with AUC 0.995 (95% CI 0.988-1.000), no higher than ALT alone (AUC 1.000; DeLong p = 0.23), the variable that defines this outcome. Against non-circular outcomes, Ferritin Day 1 discriminated shock/DSS with AUC 0.789 and severe thrombocytopenia with AUC 0.727. The ferritin-platelet inverse correlation was demographic-independent (partial Spearman rho=-0.392; p < 0.001). Ferritin offered no incremental benefit over platelet count alone (NRI = 0.143; IDI = 0.000). Serum ferritin rose from admission to hospital Day 3 and was higher in patients with shock and severe thrombocytopenia. The Ferritin-to-Platelet Ratio and the Ferritin/ALT Ratio are low-cost, but neither discriminated better than the routine test it contains (platelet count or ALT). Because platelet count and transaminases entered the ratios as the lowest and highest values of the admission, and outcomes were recorded over the whole stay, both ratios are markers of disease severity rather than predictors of later shock or severe hepatitis. Prospective multi-centre studies with laboratory values and outcomes timed from admission are needed to test any predictive role.

items.title: RETRACTION: Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis.
items.abstract: S.M. Rasheed, A.M. Abdel Monem, A.H. Abd Ellah, and M.S. Abdel Fateh, "Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis," International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics 121, no. 3(2013): 247-251, 10.1016/j.ijgo.2012.12.020. The above article, published online on 19 March 2013 in Wiley Online Library (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Michael Geary; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. UK. Concerns were raised by a third party regarding the distribution of women with liver cirrhosis between Tables 1 and 3 in the study, as they and the Child-Pugh scores all differ between these tables when the numbers should remain the same. The publisher asked the authors to clarify these inconsistencies and provide the raw data for the study. The authors did not provide the requested data but responded to the concerns. Upon review of their response, the editorial team and publisher did not feel it explained these serious concerns adequately. Subsequently, further concerns were identified, including irreproducible odds ratios, lack of a reference category, and contradictions between the confidence intervals and p-values in the tables. In addition, the journal sought a clinical opinion from an expert in the area who felt that some of the clinical findings and outcome were not consistent with the typical clinical course of the condition. As a result, the data and conclusions are considered unreliable, and therefore the article must be retracted.
items.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics

items.title: Fusion of deep and handcrafted features from multi-modal ultrasound data for multi-task liver disease diagnosis.
items.abstract: Chronic liver diseases, including fibrosis, inflammation, and steatosis, often coexist and challenge accurate diagnosis. Current approaches either carry procedural risks or fail to provide comprehensive early assessment. This study aims to develop a non-invasive, multimodal ultrasound-based framework for simultaneous grading of all three conditions. Our method integrates deep semantic features from deep learning networks with handcrafted features from quantitative ultrasound techniques, capturing complementary information from B-mode images, shear wave elastography, and radio-frequency data. Deep features can reveal discriminable and robust high-dimension non-linear relationships, while handcrafted features can capture ultrasonic characteristics related to the three diseases. These features are fused via a lightweight neural network to predict the probability of different grades of the three diseases, with liver biopsy results serving as the reference standard. The proposed method is evaluated on a cohort of 142 patients with chronic hepatitis B. The proposed method achieves AUCs of 0.86, 0.85, 0.89, and 0.93 for fibrosis staging of ≥ F1, ≥ F2, ≥ F3, and F4, respectively; 0.87 and 0.95 for inflammation grading of ≥ A2 and A3, respectively; and 0.83 and 0.93 for steatosis grading of ≥ S1 and ≥ S2, respectively. The proposed method outperforms existing methods and demonstrates robust performance in both early and advanced disease stages. This multi-task framework has potential as a clinically actionable tool for comprehensive liver disease assessment and decision support.

items.title: [Differential diagnosis of aseptic meningitis in Central Europe: An overview of less common infectious etiologies].
items.abstract: Aseptic meningoencephalitis in immunocompetent adults in Central Europe is most commonly attributed to Borrelia burgdorferi, enteroviruses, herpesviruses (HSV, VZV), and tick-borne encephalitis virus. While these agents retain diagnostic priority, a range of less common yet clinically relevant etiologies are frequently overlooked in differential diagnosis, potentially affecting disease course and patient prognosis. This narrative review focuses on such underrecognized infectious agents in patients without a travel history outside Central Europe and adjacent regions. Discussed pathogens include hepatitis E virus (particularly genotype HEV-3, with its neurological manifestations such as neuralgicamyotrophy and Guillain-Barré syndrome), acute HIV infection, neurosyphilis, leptospirosis, bartonellosis, tularemia,Rickettsia, Anaplasma, and Coxiella infections, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and Tropheryma whipplei. Particular attention is given to vector-borne neurotropic viruses relevant to the Central European region (West Nile virus, Usutu virus, Tahyna virus, Borna disease virus 1, Toscana virus, Sindbis virus, and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus), respiratory viruses (influenza, SARS-CoV-2, measles, mumps, etc.), and opportunistic pathogens in immunocompromised patients. For each pathogen, key epidemiological associations, typical clinical presentation, and recommended diagnostic approach are summarized, including limitations of serological methods (notably cross-reactivity among flaviviruses) and the potential role of next-generation metagenomic sequencing. The aim of this review is to provide clinicians with a practical tool for broadening the differential diagnosis of aseptic meningoencephalitis and to highlight epidemiological and clinical clues that may facilitate earlier recognition of these overlooked, yet treatable or prognostically significant, etiologies. Keywords: aseptic meningitis, meningoencephalitis, differential diagnosis, neuroinfection, Central Europe.

items.title: Syphilitic proctitis with profuse rectal bleeding in an HIV-infected patient with preserved CD4 count (case report).
items.abstract: Syphilitic proctitis is an uncommon and frequently under-recognized manifestation of Treponema pallidum infection that can closely mimic inflammatory, infectious, or neoplastic rectal disease. We report an unusually severe, hemorrhagic presentation in a patient with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and a preserved cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4) count, a setting in which overlapping etiologies often delay the diagnosis. A heterosexual man in his early 50s with untreated HIV infection and chronic hepatitis B-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class B) presented with sudden onset of profuse hematochezia, watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and fatigue. Computed tomography angiography revealed pronounced rectal wall thickening with deep ulceration. Colonoscopy demonstrated an indurated, ulcerated rectal lesion, and biopsy showed dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, with spirochetes confirmed by T pallidum immunohistochemistry. Negative cytomegalovirus (CMV) immunohistochemistry, undetectable CMV DNA in plasma and rectal tissue, and a preserved CD4 count (445 cells/µL) made CMV proctitis unlikely. The overall clinical, endoscopic, and histologic findings supported a diagnosis of syphilitic proctitis. Management included doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, selected because of the patient's documented penicillin allergy. Antiretroviral therapy with bictegravir/tenofovir alafenamide/emtricitabine was initiated to treat HIV and provide concurrent hepatitis B coverage. Within 2 weeks, the patient experienced complete resolution of hematochezia and diarrhea. At 3-month follow-up, the CD4 count had risen to 570 cells/µL, HIV RNA was undetectable (<20 copies/mL), and the rapid plasma reagin titer had declined from 1:512 to 1:32. This case underscores that syphilitic proctitis may manifest with severe ulcerative disease even in patients with relatively preserved immune function. Clinicians should maintain vigilance for syphilis in individuals with HIV who present with rectal bleeding or proctitis to prevent diagnostic delays and ensure timely therapy.

items.title: Predictors and prognostic impact of spontaneous portal vein thrombosis recanalization in cirrhosis: An individual patient data meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Portal vein thrombosis (PVT) in cirrhosis has a quite unpredictable natural history. Spontaneous recanalization may occur, but predictors and prognostic impact remain uncertain. We performed an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to evaluate survival according to spontaneous recanalization and to identify predictors of recanalization. We included cohort studies of patients with cirrhosis and PVT not receiving anticoagulation and obtained de-identified IPD. All-cause mortality was analyzed using a competing-risk model (competing event: liver transplantation) adjusted for prespecified baseline covariates. Predictors of recanalization were assessed with mixed-effects ordinal logistic regression including a random study intercept. Eight studies contributed 586 patients. Spontaneous recanalization occurred in 264 (47.7%). Overall recanalization was independently associated with lower mortality (aSHR 0.51; 95% CI 0.28-0.90), with the benefit driven by complete recanalization (aSHR 0.45; 95% CI 0.21-0.94). Recanalization of PVT localized in the main portal vein trunk was linked to a strong survival benefit (interaction SHR 0.39; 95% CI 0.16-0.91; p=0.02), whereas no benefit was observed after recanalization of isolated intrahepatic branch thrombosis. PVT recanalization was more likely to occur in Child-Pugh A (aOR 2.63; 95% CI 1.18-5.88), partial thrombosis (aOR 1.69; 95% CI 1.09-2.56), and isolated intrahepatic location (aOR 2.04; 95% CI 1.23-3.33). Spontaneous recanalization occurs in approximately half of patients with cirrhosis and PVT and is associated with improved survival, particularly when complete and involving the main portal vein trunk. These findings underscore its prognostic relevance and indirectly support anticoagulation to promote recanalization.

items.title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

items.title: Plain language summary: comparing ivonescimab plus chemotherapy with placebo plus chemotherapy in people with advanced EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose disease worsened on EGFR-TKI treatment in the HARMONi study.
items.abstract: What is this summary about? HARMONi is a study of a new treatment for people with advanced or metastatic non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with an activating mutation in the epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR ) gene. The study included participants in Asia, Europe, and North America whose cancer had gotten worse after treatment with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI). Ivonescimab is a new type of cancer treatment that helps the immune system recognize and attack tumor cells. It also blocks the formation of new blood vessels that tumors need to grow. HARMONi compared ivonescimab plus chemotherapy with placebo plus chemotherapy. What were the results? Participants who were given ivonescimab plus chemotherapy lived longer without their cancer getting worse or spreading (called progression-free survival ). The median progression-free survival was 6.8 months with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy compared with 4.4 months with placebo plus chemotherapy. This difference was statistically significant . The median overall survival , or the amount of time participants lived after starting treatment, was longer with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy (median, 16.8 months) compared with placebo plus chemotherapy (median, 14.0 months); however, this difference was not statistically significant.Two hundred and seven of 218 participants (95%, or about 9 out of every 10) who were given ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and 203 of 218 participants (93%, or about 9 out of every 10) who were given placebo plus chemotherapy had side effects related to their treatment. Common side effects with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy included changes in blood cell levels, nausea, decreased appetite, vomiting, and changes in liver enzymes. Some participants in each treatment group had severe or serious side effects . Four participants who received ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and five who received placebo plus chemotherapy died from treatment-related side effects. What do the results mean? For participants whose advanced NSCLC had gotten worse after EGFR-TKI treatment, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy resulted in a reduced risk of cancer getting worse or spreading by nearly half, compared with placebo plus chemotherapy. Overall survival was longer with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy; however, the difference was not statistically significant. Side effects occurred in a similar proportion of participants in both treatment groups. Most side effects could be managed without significantly impacting the participants’ quality of life or requiring treatment discontinuation. Clinical trial number : NCT06396065.

items.title: Imaging characteristics of orbital involvement in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms: a report of two cases.
items.abstract: This case series presents clinical and radiological findings of two patients with orbital involvement of neuroendocrine neoplasm (NEN) and discusses imaging characteristics in the context of modern literature.Full ophthalmic examination and orthoptic assessment were completed in two patients. Magnetic resonance imaging of the orbit and brain was carried out using 1.5 Tesla MRI (Siemens Symphony, Erlangen, Germany)Despite different systemic involvement (Patient 1: primary lesion in the caecum, with multiple deposits in the liver, left iliac crest, myocardium, pleura, paratracheal region and paraoesophageal nodes; patient 2: skin and pituitary lesions) in all patients in this case series, orbital MRI showed a lobulated, well-circumscribed lesion adherent or involving extraocular muscles. In both cases, orbital involvement was not isolated. Brain and scalp lesions in patient 2 had similar lobulated heterogeneous appearance.This case series highlights the importance of systemic work-up of patients presenting with NEN to assess for both primary and extent of disease. Multi-disciplinary team involvement is essential to provide patients with a correct diagnosis and appropriate management promptly.
